1.title: Asakusa Engei Hall: Early, Middle and Late September Programs
1.summary: Regular September performances featuring rakugo, manzai and variety acts. Daytime and evening shows are held every day.
1.body:
## Asakusa Engei Hall: Early, Middle and Late September Programs

This September, Asakusa Engei Hall will once again hold its regular performances every day without a break, featuring a diverse lineup of rakugo, manzai and variety acts (iromono). The program changes every ten days: the **early program (Kamiseki)** runs from the 1st to the 10th, the **middle program (Nakaseki)** from the 11th to the 20th, and the **late program (Shimoseki)** from the 21st to the 30th, so the lineup of performers changes three times over the course of the month.

This means that even within the same month, you can see different performers and acts depending on when you visit. Regulars and first-time visitors to a yose theater alike are sure to find something fresh to discover.

Performances are held in **two shows a day**: the daytime show starts at **11:40**, and the evening show starts at **16:40**. You can choose either show to suit your schedule, whether on your way home from work or during free time on a day off.

From the subtle art of rakugo storytelling to the light, witty banter of manzai and the wide range of skills unique to variety acts, you can enjoy a richly varied entertainment experience in a single visit. This is especially recommended for those who want to spend a relaxed time laughing amid Asakusa's old-town atmosphere.

Checking the program schedule for the early, middle and late programs in advance and visiting on a day when your favorite performer appears is another way to enjoy the theater like a true yose aficionado.

2.title: Hanayashiki Autumn Stage Show
2.summary: An autumn-only stage show is being held at Hanayashiza Theater.
2.body:
## Hanayashiki Autumn Stage Show

A special stage show available only this autumn will be held at Hanayashiza, the theater inside Asakusa Hanayashiki. Hanayashiza has long been a favorite of families and tourists throughout the year, and this seasonal-only event features a program with a special feel that sets it apart from the usual.

One of the highlights of this event is that the **content changes daily**: depending on the day, you may see a hero show or a glamorous idol stage. Since you may see a different performance each time you visit, coming several times during the period is one way to enjoy it. The powerful hero shows are likely to be popular with children, while the idol stages look set to attract fans of a wide range of generations.

Best of all, this special stage can be **watched with park admission only**, so you can enjoy it casually without worrying about extra fees. It promises to add a little special memory to an autumn day spent at this amusement park full of Asakusa's downtown charm.

Why not visit Hanayashiki as an autumn outing with your family and friends?

3.title: Asakusa ROX Autumn Sale
3.summary: Autumn items up to 50% off at shops throughout the building.
3.body: The long-awaited autumn sale is starting at shops throughout Asakusa ROX. A wide range of autumn items, from fashion to everyday goods, are included, and you can buy them at prices up to 50% off. It is a great time for anyone thinking about switching their wardrobe for the changing season, as well as for those who want to get a head start on putting together autumn and winter outfits. With such a variety of shops in the building, browsing the floors in search of a favorite piece or accessory should be enjoyable in itself. In addition, a points-up campaign is being held at the same time during the sale period, giving you a chance to earn points more advantageously than usual. If you make smart use of your points along with your sale purchases, your future shopping will be even more economical. When you visit the Asakusa area, why not stop by Asakusa ROX and look for a new autumn staple? Quantities and the sale period may be limited, so if there is an item you are interested in, we recommend checking it out early.

4.title: Senso-ji Kiku Kuyo-e (Chrysanthemum Memorial Service)
4.summary: A traditional event offering chrysanthemum flowers, featuring the Golden Dragon Dance.
4.body:
The **Kiku Kuyo-e (Chrysanthemum Memorial Service)**, a beloved seasonal tradition that adds color to autumn at Senso-ji, is held every year on October 18 on the temple grounds. Worshippers bring chrysanthemums they have carefully tended and offer them to Kannon, praying with gratitude for daily blessings and for good health.

After the service, the offered chrysanthemums are exchanged on the spot for fresh ones. It is said that displaying the chrysanthemums you take home at the entrance of your house and similar places wards off evil spirits, so many people look forward to this exchange. Chrysanthemums of every color line the grounds, creating a scene in which the crisp fragrance of the flowers evokes the deepening of autumn.

## Highlight: The Golden Dragon Dance

One of the highlights of the event is the powerful **Golden Dragon Dance** performed on the temple grounds. The sight of the golden, gleaming dragon dancing to the sound of flutes and drums is full of impact and never fails to captivate worshippers and tourists alike. Being able to enjoy the contrasting charms of the quiet beauty of the chrysanthemums and the dynamic dance of the golden dragon at the same time is truly the special appeal of this event.

Handed down through a long history, the Kiku Kuyo-e is also an important milestone that heralds the arrival of autumn in Asakusa. Why not visit Senso-ji with plenty of time to spare on the day, and spend a moment surrounded by the scent of chrysanthemums as you watch the Golden Dragon Dance?

5.title: Asakusa Shrine Announces Autumn Festival Information
5.summary: Asakusa Shrine has published its autumn festival schedule.
5.body: Asakusa Shrine has published on its official website the schedule of ceremonies for its autumn grand festival. The autumn festival of Asakusa Shrine, beloved as the local guardian deity, is an annual event that marks the turning of the seasons, and many worshippers and local residents look forward to it every year. What has been announced this time is the schedule of the series of ceremonies associated with the festival, giving visitors an advance look at the flow of the Shinto rituals held on the shrine grounds. If you are planning to visit or watch, checking the schedule beforehand should make it easier to plan your movements on the day. For details on the schedule and order of ceremonies, please refer to the annual festival page on the official Asakusa Shrine website. As an opportunity to experience traditional Shinto rituals in the crisp autumn air, this is information not to be missed, not only for nearby residents but also for tourists visiting Asakusa. Since the information on the official website may be changed from time to time, we recommend checking the latest details again before your visit.

6.title: Ekimise Japanese Sweets POP UP Store
6.summary: Popular Japanese confectionery shops from across the country take turns opening stalls, with a new lineup every week.
6.body:
## Ekimise Japanese Sweets POP UP Store

A POP UP store that Japanese sweets lovers won't want to miss is now being held at the special venue on the 1st floor of Asakusa Ekimise. Hand-picked popular Japanese confectionery shops from all over the country gather here, offering a "weekly-changing" treat, rather than a daily-changing one. Because the lineup changes with each visit, there is always something new to discover no matter how many times you come.

Many limited-edition items available only at the venue are also on offer, making the selection perfect for anyone looking for a travel memento or a small souvenir. The lineup ranges widely from the traditional flavors of long-established shops to trendy, creative Japanese sweets, making this an event that fans of sweets-shop hopping should not miss.

Its convenient location, where you can stop by during a stroll around Asakusa, is another welcome point, and the ease of dropping in while out shopping is part of the appeal. Paying attention to the weekly changes and wondering which shop will appear next may be another fun way to enjoy it.

Why not take this opportunity to enjoy the charms of Japanese sweets from across the country here in Asakusa?

7.title: Matsuya Asakusa: Ukiyo-e and Contemporary Art Exhibition
7.summary: An exhibition of ukiyo-e associated with Asakusa alongside works by contemporary artists.
7.body: An exhibition themed around ukiyo-e and contemporary art is being held at the event space of Matsuya Asakusa. The venue displays a collection of ukiyo-e works connected to Asakusa side by side with pieces by contemporary artists, creating a layout that evokes the resonance of expression across the ages. With the delicate linework and colors of ukiyo-e, which convey the atmosphere of Edo to this day, placed in the same space as contemporary art created with present-day sensibilities, visitors can enjoy moving back and forth between the perspectives of two different eras. Set against the cultural heritage nurtured in the Asakusa area, it is also an opportunity to consider how the old and the new resonate with each other. Care also seems to have been taken with the timing of exhibit changes and the arrangement of the works, making this an exhibition best enjoyed by walking slowly and comparing the pieces carefully. Admission is free, which makes it easy to drop in on a whim. Why not take a short detour during your stroll around Asakusa and spend some time experiencing art?

8.title: [Asakusa] Specialty Coffee Shop "ASAKUSA ROAST" to Open on September 10
8.summary: An in-house roasting specialty coffee shop opens in Asakusa Rokku.
8.body:
## [Asakusa] Specialty Coffee Shop "ASAKUSA ROAST" to Open on September 10

Asakusa Rokku has long been lined with entertainment attractions and theaters, and it remains a popular area for strolling, full of old downtown (shitamachi) atmosphere. On September 10, a new coffee spot, "ASAKUSA ROAST," will open in a corner of this neighborhood.

Its **greatest feature** is its commitment to in-house roasting: beans are carefully roasted on a roaster installed inside the shop. Visitors can enjoy the fragrant aroma of roasting and watch the beans being roasted live.

The shop serves **light-roast coffee**, promising a cup that brings out the beans' natural flavor and bright acidity. Its original sweets are also not to be missed, and you can probably enjoy combinations carefully designed to pair well with the coffee.

The location is ideal for taking a break during your Asakusa sightseeing, or as a starting or ending point for a stroll. As a new spot where you can casually enjoy the world of specialty coffee made with locally sourced ingredients, its future developments are likely to draw attention.

On opening day, you may see many coffee lovers coming to get a freshly roasted cup. Asakusa is about to gain yet another new attraction.

9.title: Long-Established Tableware Shop in Nishi-Asakusa to Close at End of September
9.summary: The tableware shop, which has been in business for over 50 years, will close on September 30.
9.body: A tableware shop that has kept its noren curtain hanging in a corner of Nishi-Asakusa for more than half a century will quietly close its doors on September 30 this month. Long loved by local people who came for the rice bowls and plates that brighten everyday dining tables, the shop has stood alongside the lives of many regular customers as times have changed. Half a century is enough time for a single shop to become part of the very landscape of a neighborhood, and many will surely be sorry to hear the news of its closing. A closing sale is currently underway, offering the last chance to pick up the items the shop has carried for so many years. The tableware lined up on well-worn wooden shelves quietly carries the weight of the years the shop has accumulated. If you are walking around the Nishi-Asakusa area, please stop by and enjoy chatting with the owner and browsing the wares. The day is drawing near to say farewell, with gratitude, to this long-established shop that has supported the local community for so long.

10.title: Asakusa Public Hall Hanagata Kabuki Performance
10.summary: A kabuki performance featuring rising young star actors will be held in October.
10.body:
## Asakusa Public Hall Hanagata Kabuki Performance

A kabuki performance bringing together rising young star actors will be held this October at Asakusa Public Hall. It promises to be a valuable opportunity to enjoy up close the passionate performances of the next generation as they take on traditional repertoire.

The performance is organized in **two parts: a daytime show and an evening show**. You can enjoy it during the day, or stop by the evening show on your way home from work, so you can choose a viewing time that fits your own lifestyle.

The stage, woven from youthful energy and solid skills backed by rigorous rehearsal, is sure to be well worth seeing for longtime kabuki fans and first-time visitors alike.

Asakusa Public Hall is located in the Asakusa neighborhood, full of old downtown (shitamachi) charm, so we recommend strolling around the area and enjoying street food before or after the performance.

Tickets are scheduled to go on sale **from mid-September**. As this is a performance featuring popular programs and actors, it is wise to check information early and get ready to make your reservation.

Why not spend an autumn day immersed in the glamorous world of Hanagata Kabuki, together with the atmosphere of Asakusa?

11.title: Part of Asakusa Underground Mall Renovated
11.summary: A section of the Asakusa Underground Mall has finished renovations and reopened for business.
11.body: Renovation work on a section of the Asakusa Underground Mall, known as Japan's oldest underground shopping arcade, has recently been completed, and the area has finally reopened for business. The passageways and storefronts, which strongly retain the atmosphere of the Showa era, have always given visitors a sense of nostalgia, so there are likely many regular customers who have been eagerly awaiting this renewal. The renovation adds two new restaurants, bringing a fresh touch of color to the lineup of the mall as a whole. The way the long-loved traditional look and the newly reborn space coexist is a charm unique to this underground mall. If you stop by while strolling around Asakusa, you are sure to make new discoveries amid the retro atmosphere. Between shopping and dining, why not take a peek at the renovated section? It is likely to become a new place to take a break, not only for local residents but also for tourists visiting Asakusa. If further renovations continue in the future, they are expected to help revitalize the entire underground mall.

12.title: Taito City Launches Autumn Tourism Campaign
12.summary: Autumn tourism initiatives, including a stamp rally touring the ward.
12.body:
## Taito City Launches Autumn Tourism Campaign

Taito City has launched a tourism campaign timed for the autumn sightseeing season. The highlight is a **stamp rally** that takes place across the ward, including the Asakusa area, in which participants collect stamps as they visit multiple stops.

The walking routes combine the familiar atmosphere of Asakusa with attractions in various parts of the ward, and are designed to encourage visitors to stop by places they might not usually visit. Events run in cooperation with local shopping streets are also being held, adding the fun of visiting local shops, so visitors can enjoy both sightseeing and shopping.

Collecting stamps while strolling at a relaxed pace through the old downtown (shitamachi) streets in the crisp autumn air is a way to spend the day that families and friends alike can enjoy. It also looks set to be an opportunity for local shopping streets to meet and interact with new visitors.

Through this initiative, Taito City appears to be aiming to revitalize the community by encouraging visitors to tour the ward and to improve tourist circulation. This autumn, why not take part in this stamp rally while exploring Asakusa, and rediscover the charms of the ward?

13.title: Nakamise Weekend-Only Marché
13.summary: A weekend-only marché with goods for sale will be held on the Nakamise shopping street.
13.body: A special weekend-only space will be set up on Asakusa's Nakamise shopping street, where a marché full of local flavor will take place. On offer will be limited-edition items unique to local shops that are not usually found in stores, as well as a wide variety of street food that is an essential part of strolling around Asakusa. With a diverse lineup of stalls, from long-established flavors to new tastes, the marché is likely to create a lively atmosphere that will tempt you to drop by during your walk around Asakusa. It will be a must-see event both for those who can't decide on souvenirs and for those who want to enjoy street food. Since the event is held on weekends only, be careful not to miss your chance to visit. With the marché's festive charm added to Nakamise's characteristic energy, the street is likely to be enveloped in an even more bustling atmosphere. Why not enjoy shopping and street food while savoring a relaxing weekend moment in Asakusa?

14.title: New Lifestyle Goods Brand Opens at Asakusa ROX
14.summary: A new lifestyle goods brand shop has opened on the 3rd floor.
14.body: A new brand shop themed around lifestyle goods has recently opened on the 3rd floor of Asakusa ROX. The shop carries a wide range of items that fit into everyday life, and shoppers looking for products that combine practicality and design have already been spotted there. With this new addition adding color to a corner of the building, the flow of foot traffic throughout the entire floor is likely to improve even further. To celebrate the opening, novelty gifts are currently being handed out, and a small bonus has been prepared for visitors. When you visit Asakusa ROX, be sure to stop by and take your time browsing the variety of goods on display. You may find a new favorite item while you shop. Since supplies of the novelty gifts are expected to be limited, we recommend visiting early if you are thinking of going. We will also be keeping an eye on the future developments of this new brand, which adds a new option to the local daily life.

15.title: EN The HOUSE Asakusa Nitenmon Opens
15.summary: The apartment hotel "EN The HOUSE Asakusa Nitenmon" opened on June 24, 2026, in the Nitenmon area of Asakusa.
15.body:
## EN The HOUSE Asakusa Nitenmon Opens

A new apartment hotel, **EN The HOUSE Asakusa Nitenmon**, has been born in a corner of Asakusa close to Nitenmon Gate. It opened on June 24, 2026, adding a new option for staying in this area full of old-town Tokyo atmosphere. It has also been featured in an article by the Asakusa Tourism Federation, and has been quietly attracting attention in the local area since shortly after its opening.

The facility is characterized by apartment-style rooms equipped with a kitchen and living area, and is designed to be easy to use not only for travelers but also for long-stay guests. In addition to sightseeing stays, it is likely to be a reliable option for those who want to enjoy a workation or experience living in Asakusa.

The area around Nitenmon is popular as a base for visiting Senso-ji and Asakusa Shrine and for strolling around the old downtown, and being located nearby is expected to be a great convenience for visitors. In the Asakusa area, where accommodations for long stays have been limited until now, the addition of this new type of facility is expected to further broaden the range of ways to stay.

It has already shown a presence significant enough to be introduced by a local tourism organization, and attention is turning to what impact it will have on future accommodation demand in the Asakusa area. If you are looking for a base for sightseeing in Asakusa, why not consider "EN The HOUSE Asakusa Nitenmon" as a candidate for your next trip?

16.title: Official Website of the Kaminarimon Tawara Shopping Association Gets a Redesign
16.summary: The Kaminarimon Tawara Shopping Association, just steps from Tawaramachi Station on the Ginza Line, has launched a newly redesigned official website.
16.body: The Kaminarimon Tawara Shopping Association is located in a convenient spot right outside the exit of Tawaramachi Station on the Tokyo Metro Ginza Line, and has long supported local shops and events. Its official website has now been completely redesigned, making it easier to read and easier to find information. The new pages provide timely updates on the latest news from the association, making it easier than ever to see what is happening there now. For those who want to check out the shopping streets in the area before visiting Asakusa, it should be a reassuring source of information. The content is useful not only for people looking for local shops, but also for those who want to drop by casually while sightseeing or strolling around. Combined with the easy access from Tawaramachi Station, another attraction is that you can experience the atmosphere of the shopping association right after stepping off the train. The association's own information is expected to be updated regularly on the site going forward. If you would like to feel closer to the local community, be sure to take a look at the newly redesigned official website.

17.title: Autumn Higan-e
17.summary: A Higan memorial service held at Senso-ji on the Autumnal Equinox Day.
17.body:
## Autumn Higan-e

The Autumn Higan-e service is solemnly held at the Main Hall of Senso-ji on Autumnal Equinox Day. Higan-e is a long-standing annual observance in which people renew their feelings of gratitude and offer memorial prayers for their ancestors.

On the Autumnal Equinox Day, day and night are almost equal in length. For this reason, it is said to be a time when the world of the departed and the world of the living are more closely connected, and since ancient times it has been regarded as a fitting time to honor one's ancestors. On the day, the chanting of sutras by the monks echoes quietly through the Main Hall, and visitors burn incense and press their palms together in prayer, each with their own thoughts.

As autumn deepens in Asakusa, people can be seen visiting the temple grounds while savoring the changing of the seasons. Beyond being a **place of prayer**, it is also an opportunity for us, who are so easily caught up in the busyness of daily life, to reflect anew on our connection with family and ancestors.

If you have the chance to visit Senso-ji, why not attend this Autumn Higan-e as well and offer your prayers in a tranquil moment? In the historic district of Asakusa, you will be able to encounter a form of prayer that has been passed down unchanged.

18.title: Sho-Go-Ku Dai Goma (Great Fire Ritual)
18.summary: A great goma fire ritual held on the Fudo Myoo festival days in January, May and September.
18.body:
## Sho-Go-Ku Dai Goma (Great Fire Ritual)

On September 28, the Main Hall of Senso-ji Temple will solemnly hold the "**Sho-Go-Ku Dai Goma**." This is a special goma fire ritual performed on the Fudo Myoo festival days, which come around three times a year in January, May and September. Since ancient times, many worshippers have visited to entrust their wishes for family safety, business prosperity, protection from misfortune and more.

The flames burned on the goma altar are said to be the fire of wisdom of Fudo Myoo (Acala), and the sound of sutras chanted alongside the flickering flames brings a solemn atmosphere to the Main Hall. Repeated on each festival day rather than only once a year, this ritual is also cherished as a seasonal milestone deeply rooted in life in Asakusa.

On the day, in the Main Hall enveloped in a majestic atmosphere unlike any other, you will be able to feel up close how prayer is put into each and every movement of the monks.

As signs of autumn begin to appear, why not visit Senso-ji for worship and experience the solemn atmosphere of the Sho-Go-Ku Dai Goma? A quiet moment of pressing your hands together in prayer, away from the daily hustle and bustle, should be a valuable opportunity to calm your mind.

19.title: Jūya-e (Ten Nights Service)
19.summary: A nenbutsu Buddhist service in which "Jōgyō Zanmai" is performed in the Main Hall.
19.body:
## Jūya-e (Ten Nights Service)

Held every autumn at Senso-ji, the "Jūya-e" is a Buddhist service in which participants praise the virtues of Amida Buddha and quietly practice while chanting the nenbutsu. Originally the event is held over a long period of ten days and nights, but at Senso-ji it is condensed into a single day, **October 17**, and performed in the Main Hall.

On the day, following the ritual of "Jōgyō Zanmai," monks continuously chant the nenbutsu before the principal image enshrined in the Main Hall, creating a solemn atmosphere. In the usually bustling town of Asakusa, this is the one day when a calm and solemn air fills the Main Hall, and visitors will find themselves listening closely to the sound of the chanting.

Held in a season when the deepening of autumn can be felt, this service offers a moment to step away from the hectic everyday routine, press your hands together, and settle your mind. If you have the chance to visit Asakusa, please stop by the Main Hall and experience the voices of the nenbutsu that have been passed down since ancient times.

21.title: Shakyo Kuyo-e (Jushu Kuyo) – Memorial Service for Sutra Copies
21.summary: A Buddhist service held to memorialize sutra copies that have been offered.
21.body:
## Shakyo Kuyo-e (Jushu Kuyo) – Memorial Service for Sutra Copies

On October 29, a Shakyo Kuyo-e (Jushu Kuyo) memorial service for sutra copies will be held in the Main Hall of Senso-ji Temple. In this ceremony, sutra copies offered by worshippers and devotees with their daily prayers are respectfully burned and memorialized before the sacred altar. It is one of Senso-ji's important annual events, passed down since ancient times.

Sutra copying (shakyo) has long been practiced as a part of Buddhist training. Senso-ji accepts sutra copies year-round, and this memorial service is the culmination of that practice. Each sutra copy carries the wishes and feelings of the person who wrote it. By memorializing them through the solemn rites of the **Jushu Kuyo** (Ten Types of Offerings), the prayers embodied in the sutra copies are said to be joined with the Buddhist bond.

The sound of sutra chanting echoes quietly through the Main Hall, and the service proceeds in the solemn atmosphere that fills the hall. Visitors can watch the service and experience one side of Senso-ji in autumn amid a tranquil atmosphere.

Held in the clear autumn air, this memorial service offers a moment to step away from the bustle of daily life and quietly press your hands together in prayer. Not only those familiar with sutra copying, but also the many visitors to Senso-ji will find it a fine opportunity to calm the mind and offer a prayer.

If you plan to visit Asakusa on that day, we invite you to stop by the Main Hall and experience this solemn service.

22.title: Shirasagi no Mai (White Heron Dance)
22.summary: An elegant White Heron Dance performed on the temple grounds.
22.body:
## Shirasagi no Mai (White Heron Dance)

When the dancers, dressed in white costumes, quietly appear on the spacious grounds of Senso-ji, the air seems to grow crisp and still. This year again, the White Heron Dance will be performed on the temple grounds on **November 3**.

True to its name, the White Heron Dance is a traditional performing art in which dancers wear costumes modeled after a bird spreading its wings, and show graceful footwork in time with the sounds of flutes and drums. Because it is a rare performance presented only a few times a year, not a few worshippers are said to be eagerly awaiting the day.

Every slow, measured movement of the dance carries forms handed down through a long history, quietly moving those who watch. The unique solemn atmosphere created by the majestic setting of the temple grounds is also one of the highlights.

In the clear autumn air, the sight of white feathered robes fluttering will feel like gazing at a picture scroll. If you are planning to visit Asakusa, we hope you will take this opportunity to see this tradition-filled dance from beginning to end.

23.title: Shichi-Go-San Kaji-e Blessing Ceremony
23.summary: A blessing ceremony praying for children's growth, centered on the 15th.
23.body:
## Shichi-Go-San Kaji-e Blessing Ceremony

Once November arrives, families visiting shrines and temples for Shichi-Go-San become a common sight in Asakusa. Held in the Main Hall of Senso-ji Temple during a period centered on the 15th, the **Shichi-Go-San Kaji-e** is one of the local events that has long been cherished in the community.

The sight of children dressed in festive kimono and haori hakama, led by the hand toward the Main Hall by their families with slightly nervous expressions, is a heartwarming scene unique to this season.

At the Kaji-e, monks perform prayers, giving thanks for the children's growth so far and praying for their healthy growth in the years ahead. As the solemn sound of sutra chanting echoes through the Main Hall, the families quietly pressing their palms together convey a warm and caring gaze toward their children.

Because the ceremony is **held every day** during the period, visitors can choose a convenient day to pay their respects, which makes it easy to attend. Why not offer your prayers at the historic Senso-ji Temple to mark this milestone in life, Shichi-Go-San?

24.title: Jodo-e (Buddha's Enlightenment Day)
24.summary: A Buddhist ceremony celebrating the Buddha's attainment of enlightenment.
24.body:
## Jodo-e (Buddha's Enlightenment Day)

On December 8, the Jodo-e ceremony is solemnly held in the Main Hall of Senso-ji Temple. This annual event commemorates the Buddha's attainment of enlightenment after long years of ascetic practice, and celebrates it while reflecting on his revered figure.

At this time of year, when the bustle of the year-end season begins to fill the streets, a quiet and pure atmosphere fills the Main Hall, giving worshippers a chance to collect their thoughts once more before the year comes to a close.

Jodo-e is regarded as one of the important ceremonies related to the life of the Buddha, alongside **Hana Matsuri (Flower Festival)** and **Nehan-e (Nirvana Ceremony)**, and it is also a valuable opportunity to contemplate "enlightenment," the fundamental event in Buddhism. The ceremony held in the majestic Main Hall of Senso-ji conveys to the present day the form of faith that has been passed down in this place since ancient times, giving visitors a sense of solemnity.

Perhaps the very busiest days of the year-end are the best time to experience such a traditional event and quietly press your hands together in prayer. When you visit Asakusa, please stop by the Main Hall and feel the atmosphere of Jodo-e for yourself.

25.title: Hagoita-ichi (Battledore Fair) / Osame no Kannon Festival Day
25.summary: The traditional year-end Hagoita-ichi (Battledore Fair) is held on the temple grounds.
25.body:
## Hagoita-ichi (Battledore Fair) / Osame no Kannon Festival Day

A beloved seasonal tradition that brightens Senso-ji Temple at the end of the year is the **Hagoita-ichi (Battledore Fair)**, held on the temple grounds. This year, for **three days from December 17 to 19**, stalls selling lucky hagoita battledores will line the grounds. The sight of colorful oshie (padded-fabric relief) hagoita on display adds the festive splendor that is typical of Asakusa in December.

The Hagoita-ichi is a traditional event that has continued since the Edo period, and the custom of buying a hagoita as a New Year decoration is still carried on today. From decorative hagoita modeled on kabuki actors and people in the news, to traditional designs celebrating a child's first New Year, part of the fair's charm is that it is enjoyable just to stroll and look.

Also on **the 18th**, the "Osame no Kannon Festival Day" (the final Kannon festival day of the year) will be held. Fitting for the close of the year, many worshippers come to offer their thanks to Kannon. Lively calls from shoppers choosing their hagoita mingle with worshippers quietly pressing their hands together in prayer within the same grounds, a scene unique to this time of year.

At night, the illuminated grounds are enveloped in a magical atmosphere and show a different face from the daytime. The fair lasts only three days, but that makes for an especially lively atmosphere amid the hustle and bustle of the year's end.

As the cold deepens, why not dress warmly and come to savor Asakusa's winter tradition at a leisurely pace? Picking up a lucky hagoita is also a great way to prepare for welcoming the new year.

26.title: Joya no Kane (Tenda Kuyo-e) – New Year's Eve Bell Ringing
26.summary: The New Year's Eve bell ringing held at Benten-yama.
26.body:
## Joya no Kane (Tenda Kuyo-e) – New Year's Eve Bell Ringing

On New Year's Eve night, Benten-yama, located within the grounds of Senso-ji, hosts the Tenda Kuyo-e, also known as Joya no Kane, the bell ringing that closes out the year. The solemn sound of the bell is said to **dispel the 108 earthly desires**. Each strike echoes through the hushed temple grounds and quietly cleanses the hearts of worshippers.

As the bell rings out, the grounds fill with people who also come for their first shrine and temple visit of the year, and the approach from Kaminarimon to the main hall is wrapped in the excitement of the year's end. Listening to the lingering resonance of the bell in the chilly December air while looking back on the year gone by is a scene unique to Asakusa at year's end.

This event, handed down since long ago, is also an important milestone for local people as they welcome the new year. On the faces of those gathered in the grounds, gratitude for the past year mingles with hope for the new one, and a solemn atmosphere lingers along with the sound of the bell.

Even amid the bustle of the year's end, this is a moment when you may wish to stop, and put your hands together in quiet prayer. When you visit Asakusa, why not listen to the bell at Benten-yama and savor the close of the year?

27.title: Taito City Junior Orchestra 44th Regular Concert
27.summary: The Taito City Junior Orchestra will hold its regular concert at Asakusa Public Hall.
27.body: Organized by the Lifelong Learning Division of the Taito City Board of Education, the Junior Orchestra regular concert, where local children showcase the results of their everyday practice, will be held again this year at Asakusa Public Hall. Now in its 44th year, this long-standing concert features members who enjoy music here in Taito City, and their performances, played with hearts in harmony, draw large audiences every time. Seeing young people earnestly devote themselves to their instruments, and the moment when their repeated practice pays off, is sure to leave viewers with a refreshing sense of emotion. Admission is free, making it easy to drop by. However, a numbered ticket is required for entry, so if you plan to attend, please be sure to prepare in advance. Having supported community-rooted music activities for many years, this concert is also cherished as a place to watch children grow. For those who want to spend a moment of autumn in the Asakusa area, or who want to experience the local music culture, it looks to be a day not to be missed. It is also a recommended event for families and those visiting with children.

28.title: Ito Shiro Ichiza Returns!? at Asakusa Public Hall
28.summary: Screenings of two early works by Ito Shiro Ichiza, plus a hilarious talk event with Ito Shiro, Miyake Yuji and Tokyo Kandenchi.
28.body: Presented by Ticket Space, "Ito Shiro Ichiza Returns!?" will be held at Asakusa Public Hall. The highlight this time is a rare screening of two early works created when Ito Shiro Ichiza was still just getting started. 29.title: Soichi Futami Yamabiko Concert 2026 in Tokyo
29.summary: A kayokyoku concert by Soichi Futami will be held.
29.body: "Soichi Futami Yamabiko Concert 2026 in Tokyo" is drawing attention as a kayokyoku (Japanese popular song) stage that adds color to autumn in Asakusa. Soichi Futami, who continues his career with a rich, powerful singing voice, will reunite with his fans in Tokyo in this one-night-only concert. We hope you will experience the moment when Soichi Futami's voice resounds, in person at the venue. We recommend securing your tickets early.

32.title: JUST JESUS DAGAYO Worship Service

## JUST JESUS DAGAYO Worship Service

33.title: Asakusa Music Festival 2026 Night 1: Asakusa "Summer" Wind Band Festival
33.summary: The first night of the Asakusa Music Festival 2026, bringing together wind band groups, will take place.
33.body:
## Asakusa Music Festival 2026 Night 1: Asakusa "Summer" Wind Band Festival

The sounds of wind bands will fill the streets of Asakusa as the "Asakusa Music Festival 2026" finally reaches its first night. Titled the Asakusa "Summer" Wind Band Festival, this event brings together local wind band groups, each presenting the performances they have honed.

The sound of wind bands played in the clear summer air, combined with the atmosphere of Asakusa itself, is sure to feel especially evocative. The event can be enjoyed by a wide range of people, from families with children to wind band fans, so why not come along?

34.title: The 166th Sosaku Buyo Kawafuji-ryu Joint Performance
34.summary: A joint performance by Kawafuji-ryu, a school of creative Japanese dance (Sosaku Buyo), will be held.
34.body:
## The 166th Sosaku Buyo Kawafuji-ryu Joint Performance

Kawafuji-ryu, a school of creative Japanese dance (Sosaku Buyo) that has been passed down in Asakusa for many years, will hold its 166th joint performance. The very fact that the school has reached its 166th performance speaks to the depth of its history and its steady efforts to preserve Japanese dance as a traditional performing art.

This performance is hosted by Kawafuji-ryu and will be a special stage where students who train diligently every day showcase the skills and expression they have honed. Through the program, audiences can fully enjoy the highlights unique to Japanese dance, such as the aesthetic sense embodied in every handling of the fan and every movement, and the harmony between costumes that reflect the seasons and the music.

Best of all, **admission is free** and **all seats are unreserved**, making this a performance that is easy to attend even for those unfamiliar with Japanese dance. Seats are available on a first-come, first-served basis, so if you would like a good seat, we recommend arriving at the venue with plenty of time to spare.

Being in Asakusa, you can also enjoy strolling around the area and sampling street food before or after the performance, allowing you to soak in the atmosphere of old downtown Tokyo throughout the day. We invite you to visit the venue with family and friends for this rare opportunity to experience a stage art woven from tradition and creativity.

35.title: The 10th Ogikikukai
35.summary: The 10th performance of the Japanese dance recital "Ogikikukai" will be held.
35.body:
## The 10th Ogikikukai

"Ogikikukai," a Japanese dance recital cherished as an event rooted in Asakusa, is now celebrating its milestone 10th performance. Organized by the Bando school, this recital is a special stage where performers who have devoted themselves to practice show off the fruits of their daily training, and with each edition it has drawn growing attention from performing arts fans in the local community. As this is the landmark tenth edition, the performance promises to look back on the journey so far while raising hopes for the future.

The venue is divided into the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd floors. **Unreserved seating on the 1st floor requires a paid ticket**, while **the 2nd and 3rd floor seats are open free of charge**, so you can easily drop in and experience the world of Japanese dance.

Japanese dance, woven from graceful movements and refined gestures, has a charm that quietly draws in those who watch it. Whether you are familiar with traditional performing arts or seeing Japanese dance for the first time, Ogikikukai's carefully crafted stage is sure to offer new discoveries. Set in Asakusa, it is expected to be a luxurious time to fully savor the atmosphere of traditional Japan.

Why not visit the venue on an autumn day and take in the many dances that will adorn this 10th milestone?

36.title: Akira Kohama 70th Birthday Concert
36.summary: A concert celebrating Akira Kohama's 70th birthday will be held.
36.body:
## Akira Kohama 70th Birthday Concert

For local fans in Asakusa, this is a night not to be missed: the Akira Kohama 70th Birthday Concert. Planned as a special stage celebrating a milestone for an artist who has continued his musical career for many years, it promises to be a valuable opportunity to look back on his journey so far.

37.title: Columbia Dance Parade Kanto Regional Tournament

## Columbia Dance Parade Kanto Regional Tournament

The Kanto regional tournament of the "Columbia Dance Parade," a celebration of ballroom dance held in the Asakusa area, is finally about to open, with the local community as its stage. 38.title: Toshimi Tagawa 35th Anniversary Debut Concert

39.title: President Ishida's "My Recommendation" Yume Concert
39.summary: A popular song concert hosted by Yume Group will be held.

The selection of the Asakusa ROX branch from among so many stores is happy news for the local Asakusa community as well.

51.title: ROX Parking Lot Fee Revision Notice

52.title: Munyugurumi Patio POP UP STORE Opens

54.title: Nagatanien's "Ochazuke Sambista" Appears at the Asakusa Samba Carnival

56.title: Senso-ji Temple to Hold Special Viewing of Denboin Garden and Ema-do Hall (Scenic Sites)
56.summary: The Denboin Garden and Ema-do Hall of Senso-ji Temple, normally closed to the public, will be open for special viewing from October 30 to November 3.
56.body:
## Special Viewing of Senso-ji's Scenic Sites for a Limited Time

A rare event will offer a limited-time special viewing of the Denboin Garden and Ema-do Hall, both designated as scenic sites of Senso-ji Temple. The event was announced by HITOHATA, INC.

The Denboin Garden is not normally open to the public. It is known as a strolling garden with a charm that changes with the seasons, and opportunities to see it open for this many consecutive days are by no means common. The Ema-do Hall, which will also be open, is a building that conveys the history of worshippers' prayers to this day and is well worth seeing. Viewing both together will let you experience the deeper charm of Senso-ji.

The event will run from **October 30 to November 3, 2026**, making it an ideal time of year to enjoy the garden at leisure in the clear autumn air. You may also be able to enjoy autumn foliage in the garden during the period. Spending time among the historic garden and architecture, in a quiet spot slightly removed from the bustle of Asakusa, is likely to be a precious experience for locals and tourists alike.

Because the viewing period is limited, those planning to visit should leave plenty of time in their schedules. Don't miss this special autumn opportunity to catch a glimpse of a side of Senso-ji that is usually out of sight.

58.title: Asakusa's "Tokyo Sushi Bowl" Earns Halal Certification
58.summary: "Tokyo Sushi Bowl," a restaurant in Asakusa, has obtained halal certification from the Japan Halal Foundation.
58.body: "Tokyo Sushi Bowl" in Asakusa has newly obtained halal certification from the Japan Halal Foundation. The restaurant, which serves Japanese food including sushi, has long been a local favorite. With this certification, a third-party organization has now officially verified that its ingredient selection and cooking processes comply with Islamic dietary law. This is expected to strengthen its appeal to Muslim tourists, and it can be said that an environment has been created in which even those who previously felt uneasy about dining can visit with peace of mind. Asakusa is a tourist destination visited by many travelers from Japan and abroad, and for Muslim tourists, whose dining options have been limited for religious reasons, the existence of a certified restaurant like this is a valuable choice. If similar efforts spread to nearby restaurants in the future, it may also lead to a better reception system for the Asakusa area as a whole. We hope to see the development of a town where everyone can enjoy food with peace of mind, regardless of their background or faith. When you visit the restaurant, paying attention to the efforts behind the certification may give you a different perspective on the charm of this town.

62.title: Contact Lens Store Eye City: First-Time Customer 30% OFF Campaign Ending Soon

The lineup goes beyond apparel to include a wide range of fashion accessories such as bags and accessories, with items planned to help expand your coordination options. Souvenir items unique to the Asakusa area are also said to be on display in the store, making it a place you can casually drop in on while sightseeing or strolling.

How the trend-savvy lineup, honed in Harajuku, will blend into Asakusa's streetscape full of old-town charm is another highlight, and that contrast is well worth seeing. For locals and visitors to Asakusa alike, this adds a new shopping option.

On opening day, the store is expected to be busy with shoppers who have been eagerly awaiting its debut. If you are shopping or sightseeing nearby, this is a new store worth stopping by.

70.title: Muten Kura Sushi: Limited-Time Extended Hours
70.summary: Muten Kura Sushi on the 4th floor of Asakusa ROX will extend its hours on Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays: August 21–23, September 4–6 and September 18–20.
70.body:
## Muten Kura Sushi: Limited-Time Extended Hours

Muten Kura Sushi, located on the 4th floor of Asakusa ROX, will extend its business hours on Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays: August 21–23, September 4–6 and September 18–20, 2026.

During these periods, the restaurant will open earlier than usual at **10:20** and stay open until **24:00**, a significant extension. Last entry is at 23:30 and last order is at 23:50, so if you plan to visit late at night, allow yourself plenty of time.

Regular hours are 11:00–23:00 on weekdays, and 10:20–23:00 on Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays (last entry 22:30, last order 22:50). Compared with these, the extended hours offer more convenient times for both opening and closing.

For those who want to enjoy a meal a bit later after work, or whose days are packed and can only go out at night, this is a welcome change with more options. It should also be easier to stop by while sightseeing in Asakusa or shopping at ROX.

The eligible period is limited, so it is best to check the dates in advance if you plan to visit. With the casual atmosphere of a conveyor-belt sushi restaurant, it is also well suited to families and groups of friends.

We recommend checking the details of the period and the latest information with the restaurant or official sources before your visit.

73.title: Long-Established Wagashi Shop "Funawa" Opens a Store on Cake.jp
73.summary: Funawa, a long-established Asakusa wagashi (traditional Japanese confectionery) shop founded in 1902 (Meiji 35), has opened a store on the online mall Cake.jp and begun selling items such as imo yokan (sweet potato yokan).
73.body: Funawa, a long-established wagashi shop in Asakusa that has carried on its traditions since its founding in 1902 (Meiji 35), has opened a store on Cake.jp, a sweets mail-order site operated by Cake.jp Co., Ltd. For many fans, it will be welcome news that flavors long loved by locals and tourists alike can now be enjoyed at home without visiting the shop. The signature "Imo Yokan" (sweet potato yokan) is known for its simple yet deep sweet potato flavor and has been loved across generations. The elegantly sweet "Anko Dama" (sweet bean paste balls) are also part of the lineup, making it easier to choose them as gifts or as everyday snacks. It is significant that traditional wagashi, once available only by visiting Asakusa, can now be obtained online at any time. It should also be a reassuring option for those who live far away and have had difficulty visiting, and for those who want to recall a nostalgic taste after a long time. With this new store, products that previously could only be purchased at the shop in Asakusa can now be ordered from all over Japan. By delivering the shop's traditional flavors widely through an e-commerce site, it is expected to attract new customers. Why not take this opportunity to savor at home, at your leisure, a treasure filled with the skill and history of a long-established shop?

91.title: Two-Room Hotel in an Asakusa Shopping Street Tops 80% Occupancy Within Two Months of Opening
91.summary: A small hotel with just two rooms, which opened in an Asakusa shopping street, is off to a strong start, with its occupancy rate exceeding 80% about two months after opening.
91.body: Glider Associates Co., Ltd. announced that the small two-room hotel it operates in an Asakusa shopping street has achieved an occupancy rate of over 80% about two months after opening. Small accommodations that make use of vacant shops and other spaces in shopping streets are attracting attention as a new initiative aimed at both revitalizing the local community and attracting tourists. Asakusa is an area visited by many tourists from Japan and abroad, and the hotel appears to be gaining popularity by meeting the needs of travelers seeking a unique accommodation experience. The company is reportedly also considering opening similar shopping-street-based hotels in the future, and ripple effects on the local economy are expected.

92.title: Construction Begins on Rental Residence Project in Matsugaya 4-chome, Taito-ku
92.summary: Mitsui Bussan Urban Development has begun construction of a new rental residence in Matsugaya 4-chome, Taito-ku, near Asakusa.
92.body: Mitsui Bussan Urban Development Co., Ltd. has announced that it has started construction of the new building for the "(Tentative name) Taito-ku Matsugaya 4-chome Rental Residence Project" in Matsugaya 4-chome, Taito-ku, close to the Asakusa area. Matsugaya is also close to Asakusa and Kappabashi Kitchen Town, and is being redeveloped as an area where old downtown (shitamachi) charm blends with urban functionality. The project aims to supply rental housing, and is expected to contribute to an increase in the local residential population and the revitalization of the regional economy. Details such as the completion date are expected to be announced at a later date, and the project is also drawing attention as a sign of real estate development trends around the Asakusa area.

94.title: Senso-ji Temple's 1,400th Anniversary of the Enshrinement of Its Principal Image: Asakusa Shrine Seeks Donations for the Grand Portable Shrine "Funatogyo" Boat Procession
94.summary: To commemorate the 1,400th anniversary of the manifestation of Senso-ji Temple's principal image, donations are being sought to hold a "Funatogyo" boat procession of Asakusa Shrine's grand portable shrine (miya-mikoshi).
94.body:
As Senso-ji Temple marks the major milestone of 1,400 years since the manifestation of its principal image, Asakusa Shrine plans to hold a "Funatogyo" (boat procession) of its grand portable shrine (miya-mikoshi) as a commemorative event.

Funatogyo is a Shinto ritual in which a portable shrine (mikoshi) is placed on a boat and carried across the Sumida River. It is a rare event that offers a solemn sight quite different from the usual procession on land. To hold this ritual in a special form befitting the 1,400-year milestone, Asakusa Shrine is calling widely on local residents and devotees for donations.

This initiative also carries the meaning of passing Asakusa's history and faith on to the next generation, and has become a major project involving the whole community.

For details on donations and how to apply, please check the information provided by Asakusa Shrine and the Asakusa Tourist Federation.

As a commemorative event that will go down in Asakusa's history, attention is focused on further updates.

96.title: Goku-den Susuharai & Goku-den Kaihi Hoyo (Sacred Shrine Cleaning and Door-Opening Ceremony)
96.summary: In preparation for the New Year, the soot-sweeping of the Gokuden shrine in the Main Hall and the door-opening ceremony will be held.
96.body:
## Goku-den Susuharai & Goku-den Kaihi Hoyo (Sacred Shrine Cleaning and Door-Opening Ceremony)

On December 12 and 13, Senso-ji Temple will hold the "Gokuden Susuharai" (soot-sweeping of the sacred shrine) and the "Gokuden Kaihi Hoyo" (door-opening ceremony) in the Main Hall. The Gokuden is the shrine (zushi) that enshrines the principal image. The soot-sweeping, which removes and purifies the dirt of the past year, is an important preparatory event for welcoming the New Year.

After the soot-sweeping, the door-opening ceremony is held to open the doors of the Gokuden, and the solemn interior sanctuary, which is normally not visible, is specially opened to view.

Handed down since ancient times as a seasonal feature of December, this event symbolizes the pure state of mind with which Senso-ji welcomes the new year. When visiting Asakusa at the end of the year, be sure to take note of this special ceremony as well.

98.title: Star Festival (Hoshi Kuyo-e)
98.summary: A Buddhist memorial service held in the main hall on the winter solstice, praying for good health and freedom from illness.
98.body:
## Star Festival (Hoshi Kuyo-e)

On the day of the winter solstice, the "Star Festival (Hoshi Kuyo-e)" is held in the main hall of Senso-ji Temple. The Star Festival is a traditional event in which offerings are made to one's **honmyo-sei (natal star) and toshi-sei (star of the current year)**, which are believed to govern each person's fate, and prayers are offered for good health and protection from misfortune.

The winter solstice is regarded as the day with the shortest daylight and the longest night of the year, and since ancient times it has been valued as a special turning point when yin shifts to yang. Senso-ji also holds this service to coincide with the day, and many worshippers give thanks for a safe year and pray for good health in the coming year.

Even amid the bustle of the year's end, the temple grounds are filled with a quiet and solemn atmosphere. Along with the customs of yuzu baths and pumpkin on the winter solstice, it is cherished as a traditional Japanese seasonal event.

100.title: Special Chōyō no Sekku Goshuin Now Available
100.summary: Asakusa Shrine has begun offering a special goshuin (shrine stamp) themed around Chōyō no Sekku (the Chrysanthemum Festival), one of the five seasonal festivals.
100.body: Asakusa Shrine began offering a special goshuin themed around Chōyō no Sekku on September 6, 2026. Chōyō no Sekku is one of the five seasonal festivals (Gosekku), in which chrysanthemum flowers are used to pray for longevity and eternal youth, and the goshuin incorporates this design. After worshipping at the main hall, visitors can receive the goshuin at the amulet office. As a limited-edition goshuin that lets visitors feel the change of seasons, it is expected to be popular among those who enjoy collecting goshuin. Asakusa Shrine distributes special seasonal goshuin throughout the year, and this one was planned as part of that program. Details on the distribution period and the hatsuho-ryō (offering fee) are provided from time to time on the shrine's official website. Many visitors stop by together with sightseeing in Asakusa, making this one of the topics that add color to autumn in Asakusa.

101.title: September Shakoya Event to Be Held
101.summary: Asakusa Shrine has announced the September session of "Shakoya," part of its educational activities for young people.
101.body:
Asakusa Shrine regularly holds "Shakoya," an educational program that helps children learn about Japanese customs and culture, as well as the history of Asakusa. The information for the September session has now been announced.

Shakoya is an initiative that Asakusa Shrine carries out as part of its efforts to nurture local youth, and it is held regularly as an opportunity to deepen understanding of Japanese culture and the local area. This session is the 146th, making it an activity that has taken root in the community over many years.

Those wishing to participate should apply according to the instructions in the information document (PDF). It is a valuable opportunity for local children to become familiar with Japanese culture and the history of Asakusa, and it has also drawn interest from parents.

For details such as the specific date and time and how to apply, please check the information document on the Asakusa Shrine official website.

102.title: Notice for Holders of the August 8 Worship Certificate (Suehiro Special Goshuin Exchange Ticket)
102.summary: A notice has been issued regarding the later exchange of the Suehiro Special Goshuin for worshippers who visited on August 8, Reiwa 8 and received a certificate.
102.body: Asakusa Shrine has announced an important notice about exchanges for worshippers who visited on August 8, Reiwa 8 and received a worship certificate (an exchange ticket for the Suehiro Special Goshuin, to be redeemed at a later date). Because that day was an auspicious date, many worshippers visited and crowds rushed to obtain the special goshuin, so the shrine arranged for later exchange using the certificate. Eligible holders need to receive their goshuin in accordance with the notice. Details such as the exchange method and deadline should be confirmed through Asakusa Shrine's official announcement. This is information that goshuin enthusiasts should not miss. Asakusa Shrine also plans further goshuin events tied to seasons and special dates.

103.title: Asakusa Shrine × Keikyu [Natsumode] Special Goshuin 2026
103.summary: Asakusa Shrine and Keikyu Corporation have teamed up to offer a special Natsumode goshuin (shrine stamp) for 2026.
103.body: Asakusa Shrine is offering a special Natsumode goshuin for 2026 as a collaboration project with Keikyu Corporation. Natsumode is a shrine-visiting custom held in summer, at the halfway point of the year, to express gratitude for the past six months and to pray for good health and well-being in the second half. It has been gaining popularity in recent years. This year's goshuin was created with a design that also promotes tourism along the Keikyu lines, and features motifs unique to a collaboration with a railway company. It has been offered in sequence since July 7, and has been attracting attention from visitors who enjoy collecting goshuin. Asakusa Shrine is also running a collaboration project with JR Central during the same period, and many visitors come to obtain multiple special goshuin. The number of visitors who combine a visit to the shrine with summer sightseeing in Asakusa is expected to increase.

104.title: Sponsors Sought for Restoration of the Divine Messenger Statues
104.summary: Asakusa Shrine is calling for sponsors for the restoration of the divine messenger statues on its grounds.
104.body:
Asakusa Shrine is seeking sponsorship from worshippers and local residents at large as it moves forward with a project to restore the divine messenger statues on its grounds.

The statues have been exposed to wind and rain for many years and show signs of deterioration over time, which led to the planning of this restoration project. For Asakusa Shrine, which has walked alongside the town of Asakusa, passing on to future generations these statues, which hold value as cultural properties on the grounds, is considered an important undertaking.

Details on how to sponsor and the amounts are available at the shrine's amulet office (shuyojo) and on its official website. Support is being sought from many people who cherish Asakusa's history and culture, including parishioners (ujiko) and devotees of the shrine.

Progress on the restoration is expected to be announced from time to time, and once completed, worshippers will be able to see the statues in their renewed form.

105.title: Asakusa Shrine × JR Central [Natsumode] Layered Paper-Cut Goshuin Stamp
105.summary: Asakusa Shrine is offering a special Natsumode goshuin (shrine stamp) with a layered paper-cut design, created in collaboration with JR Central.
105.body: As part of a collaboration with JR Central, Asakusa Shrine is offering a special Natsumode goshuin featuring the layered paper-cut technique. Layered paper-cutting is a technique that stacks multiple sheets of paper to create a beautiful design with a sense of depth, and this goshuin makes the most of that feature. Natsumode is an event to pray for good health and protection from illness during the second half of the year, and it is becoming established at Asakusa Shrine. Projects with railway companies are also carried out to promote tourism. Distribution is believed to have started in July, and the limited design is proving popular with worshippers seeking it. Asakusa Shrine is also offering a collaboration goshuin with Keikyu during the same period, and these collaborations with multiple companies are attracting attention. Visitors coming to tour goshuin are also expected.

106.title: Special Page on Shichi-Go-San Visits Launched
106.summary: Asakusa Shrine has launched a special page about Shichi-Go-San shrine visits.
106.body:
Asakusa Shrine has launched a special page for Shichi-Go-San, a traditional autumn event.

Shichi-Go-San is a traditional Japanese event held to pray for the healthy growth of children. Every year, many families visit Asakusa Shrine for this popular blessing. The special page is expected to provide information on how to apply for the blessing, the flow of the day, and more.

Asakusa Shrine, beloved as the guardian shrine of Asakusa, is also known for its grounds bustling with children in their festive attire during the Shichi-Go-San season. The launch of this special page is expected to make it easier for families planning to visit to prepare in advance.

Details such as the specific application period and the dates and times of the blessings are expected to be updated on the special page as they become available.

107.title: KIMONO×DANCE PROJECT Presents Stage Performance "Sakura Emi"
107.summary: "Sakura Emi," a stage performance blending kimono and dance, will be held over two days at Asakusa Public Hall.
107.body: The stage performance "Sakura Emi," presented by KIMONO×DANCE PROJECT, will be held at Asakusa Public Hall. Combining two seemingly different forms of expression, kimono and dance, the work is drawing attention as a stage where traditional beauty and modern dynamism intersect. Two performances are scheduled: on Saturday the 12th, doors open at 16:00, the show starts at 16:30, and it ends at 20:00; on Sunday the 13th, doors open at 14:00, the show starts at 14:30, and it ends at 18:00. Tickets are 5,000 yen, with all seats unreserved. The sight of the kimono's vivid colors shimmering under the stage lights, and the fabric flowing gracefully with the dancers' movements, will convey a live power that photos and videos cannot fully capture. Bringing together kimono culture and dance, this is a performance drawing attention for its fresh, new feel. For details and reservations, please check the official website of KIMONO×DANCE PROJECT.

108.title: St. Marc Café Autumn Sweet Potato Fair
108.summary: St. Marc Café is launching limited-time autumn menu items using Naruto Kintoki and Anno sweet potatoes, including Choco Cro, smoothies and a parfait.
108.body:
## St. Marc Café Autumn Sweet Potato Fair

St. Marc Café on the 1st floor of Asakusa ROX is holding a limited-time fair called "Oimo-zukushi" (All About Sweet Potatoes), featuring plenty of sweet potatoes, a taste of autumn, from September 5 to November 5, 2026. It uses sweet potatoes from several regions and varieties, including Naruto Kintoki, Anno sweet potato, Beniazuma, and sweet potatoes from Kyushu, so that you can enjoy the differences in sweetness and texture of each.

The signature item is the **"Kaoru Mitsu 'Imo' Premium Choco Cro" (390 yen, tax included)**. The sweet, silky flavor of sweet potato is sealed inside fragrant Choco Cro pastry, creating a taste that evokes autumn with every bite.

The **"Kaoru Mitsu 'Imo' Smoothie" (720 yen)**, topped with Beniazuma paste and sweet potato chips, is appealing for its smooth texture and the gentle, natural sweetness of sweet potato. It is also a great choice for a light snack.

The **"Kaoru Mitsu 'Imo' Parfait" (750 yen, dine-in only)**, generously topped with Kyushu sweet potato paste and candied sweet potato, looks like a colorful autumn treat and is a great choice for social media photos.

In addition, the **"Umami Mitsu 'Nashi' Smoothie" (690 yen)**, combined with peach jelly, joins the lineup for those who want the refreshing fruitiness and cool chill.

Why not stop by between sightseeing and shopping in Asakusa to enjoy these seasonal flavors? Please note that these items may end sales without notice depending on quantity and circumstances, so we recommend checking them out early.

109.title: CAMSHOP.JP Pop-Up Store Now Open
109.summary: CAMSHOP.JP, a goods shop themed around cars and motorcycles, opens for a limited time at the special venue on the 1st floor of ROX.
109.body:
## CAMSHOP.JP Pop-Up Store Now Open

From September 18 to October 18, 2026, "CAMSHOP.JP," which offers goods themed around cars and motorcycles, will open a shop for a limited time at the special venue on the 1st floor of Asakusa ROX. This is a physical store of the directly operated online shop run by Face Co., Ltd., making it a rare chance to see and choose in person items that are normally available only online.

The highlight is the merchandise in collaboration with the popular anime "Initial D," including wet tissue cases designed in the style of Fujiwara Tofu Shop and the AE86 Toyota Sprinter Trueno, with designs reminiscent of the vehicles in the story that will delight car and motorcycle fans. The lineup also includes **"Magnet Puzzle Badges"** (12 types, 990 yen each), which you complete by fitting the puzzle pieces together, sure to spark your collector's spirit.

The selection, aimed at those who dearly love vehicles, is appealing for combining practicality with a sense of fun. Its location, where you can drop in casually while strolling around Asakusa, is another plus, and even those unfamiliar with vehicle-themed goods may find it a good opportunity to experience this world.

Since it is open for a limited time only, be sure to check out any items that catch your eye early. The lineup can also be used to find small souvenirs for friends and family.

110.title: Asakusa Okaki Pop-Up Shop
110.summary: "Asakusa Okaki," a new specialty born in Asakusa, is opening a limited-time pop-up shop at the ROX 1F entrance, with free samples available.
110.body:
## Limited-Time Shop Now Open

"Asakusa Okaki," a new local specialty born in Asakusa this July, is opening a limited-time shop in front of the main entrance of Asakusa ROX (ROX 1F entrance) from **September 18 to September 30, 2026**.

Its key selling points are being **additive-free and gluten-free**, making it a great choice for anyone looking for a gentle, body-friendly snack. It is introduced as an okaki (Japanese rice cracker) unlike any before, with a light, crispy texture and a deep, savory umami and toasty aroma.

## How It's Sold

Okaki is sold by weight in special cups or paper bags:

- **500 yen** for 30 g in a special cup
- **1,000 yen** for 80 g in a special paper bag

You can easily buy just as much as you want to eat.

## Lineup

There are two flavors: **Genmai (brown rice)** and **Soft**. You can enjoy comparing the distinct character of each: the toasty flavor unique to brown rice, and the light, soft-textured type. Samples are also available, so you can taste before you decide.

Located right along your Asakusa sightseeing route, it looks set to be a new discovery for tourists and local regulars alike. Take a break with some okaki in hand and be sure to try Asakusa's new specialty.

Since this is a limited-time event, we recommend visiting soon.

111.title: Lingerie Noël Pop-Up Store Now Open
111.summary: Lingerie Noël, a lingerie select shop from Wacoal, is opening as a limited-time pop-up at the special venue on the 2nd floor of ROX.
111.body:
## Lingerie Noël Pop-Up Store Now Open

Lingerie Noël, a lingerie select shop run by Wacoal, will open at a special venue on the 2nd floor of Asakusa ROX for a limited time from September 3 to September 30, 2026. Its appeal lies in a wide-ranging lineup, including loungewear featuring popular characters and lingerie from "Salute," which is committed to the reliable quality that Wacoal is known for.

The shop also carries T-shirts (from 2,970 yen) designed with long-loved characters such as Tom & Jerry and Mickey Mouse, creating a pop corner that draws you in even though it is a lingerie department. In addition, a special sale on Wacoal's popular brand "Salute" is currently underway, with items available at great prices starting from 5,720 yen.

The lineup looks set to be useful not only for treating yourself but also for choosing a little gift for someone special. We hope you will enjoy a shopping experience a little different from usual, one that only a limited-time special venue can offer. If you visit ROX 2F in Asakusa, why not stop by?

114.title: Yorozu Square Limited-Time Wooden Goods Shop
114.summary: Yorozu Square, which sells wooden cutlery and magewappa (bent-wood) lunch boxes, has opened a pop-up shop in the special event space on the 1st floor of ROX.
114.body: A limited-time shop by Yorozu Square, a brand specializing in wooden goods, is open from August 14 to September 15, 2026, in the special event space on the 1st floor of Asakusa ROX. Under the concept "Make everyday meals more enjoyable," the shop offers a range of items that bring the warmth of wood, from natural wood cutlery such as spoons, forks, Chinese-style soup spoons (renge), and stirrers, to magewappa lunch boxes that add color to your daily lunch preparation. Cutlery is available at affordable prices from 110 yen to 550 yen, and magewappa lunch boxes in 500 ml and 700 ml capacities are 2,750 yen. With simple designs that make the most of the material's natural texture, the shop offers a wide variety of sizes, shapes and uses, making it a reliable choice whether you are looking for a gift or an item for everyday use. Its location on the 1st floor of ROX is also convenient for dropping in while strolling around Asakusa, so why not stop by between shopping and enjoy the scent of wood? Because this is a limited-time event in a special event space, we recommend checking out any items that catch your eye early. Why not take your time to find a special item that fits into your daily life while enjoying the warmth of wood?

115.title: Gap Store Opens on the 3rd Floor of ROX 3G
115.summary: A store of the global casual brand "Gap" will open on the 3rd floor of ROX 3G on September 18.
115.body:
## "Gap" Opens at Asakusa ROX

Asakusa ROX, a well-loved shopping spot in the Asakusa area, is getting a notable new addition this fall. "**Gap**," a global casual brand that has been popular since it was founded in San Francisco, USA, in 1969, will open on the 3rd floor of the 3G building on September 18.

True to the brand's ongoing focus on clean American casual style, the store is expected to offer simple yet trend-conscious casual items, and fashion fans have been looking forward to it even before the opening.

The store will carry a wide-ranging lineup for all ages, including **men's, women's, kids' and baby** items, so the whole family can enjoy shopping together.

Together with "WEGO," which opens around the same time, the fashion floor on the 3rd floor of Asakusa ROX 3G will be strengthened. Combined with Asakusa ROX's convenient location, it is expected to become a spot that is easy to drop into while sightseeing or shopping.

On opening day, you can also expect the lively atmosphere unique to a brand-new sales floor. It looks set to be a must-see for locals and for visitors to Asakusa alike. Why not stop by this opportunity to choose items for your new-season wardrobe?

117.title: Festival BBQ Beer Garden Asakusa EKIMISE Yatai Village
117.summary: A yatai (food stall) village offering BBQ and a beer garden is now open on the rooftop "Asakusa Hare Terrace" at EKIMISE.
117.body: At "Asakusa Hare Terrace," the rooftop space of Asakusa EKIMISE, the "Festival BBQ Beer Garden Asakusa EKIMISE Yatai Village" is now open, taking advantage of its location with a panoramic view of Tokyo Skytree. It is open 12:00–22:00 on weekdays and 11:00–22:00 on weekends and public holidays. Its highlight is that you can enjoy BBQ and all-you-can-drink menus in the lively atmosphere typical of a yatai village. From the observation deck you can see Tokyo Skytree, the tallest free-standing tower in the world, and it is attractive not only during the day but also for its illuminated night views. The open space surrounded by blue sky is also popular as a rest spot during shopping, and seasonal events are held from time to time. With its convenient location directly connected to Asakusa Station, it is expected to be used by both tourists and local customers. It is operated by Urban Earth, a company that runs outdoor barbecue facilities, and details and reservations are available on the dedicated website.

120.title: HITOHATA Produces "ASAKUSA CULTURE & LIGHTS 2026"
120.summary: "ASAKUSA CULTURE & LIGHTS 2026," an event themed around Asakusa's culture and light, will begin on October 30.
120.body:
## HITOHATA Produces "ASAKUSA CULTURE & LIGHTS 2026"

Using the entire town of Asakusa as its stage, "ASAKUSA CULTURE & LIGHTS 2026," a new event that blends the distinct appeals of traditional culture and illumination, will finally begin on October 30, 2026, produced by HITOHATA, INC.

By combining Asakusa's unique history and charm with lighting displays that color the town at night, the event reportedly aims to show visitors a side of Asakusa they have never seen before.

One of the highlights is that it can be enjoyed differently by day and by night: during the day, visitors can experience the depth of Asakusa through cultural activities, and after dusk, the streets are wrapped in soft light. The light displays set in Asakusa at night are also likely to become popular photo spots.

The event looks set to be a fresh experience for both locals and tourists. Behind the aim of creating a lively community are also hopes of revitalizing shopping streets and surrounding areas, as well as the night-time economy.

The timing suits the long autumn nights, and it is arguably the perfect season to enjoy the event while strolling through the Asakusa streets as the weather begins to cool.

Details on the venue layout and program are still to be announced, but it is an event we hope many people will visit as a chance to discover new charms of Asakusa.

121.title: Kaminarimon Bon Odori ~Yume Toro (Dream Lanterns)~ Held
121.summary: The annual Asakusa event "Kaminarimon Bon Odori ~Yume Toro (Dream Lanterns)~" was held, drawing lively crowds under a beautiful evening sky.
121.body: The Asakusa Tourism Federation's "Today's Asakusa" corner reported that the annual Kaminarimon Bon Odori ~Yume Toro (Dream Lanterns)~ has been held. The event took place on September 5, 2026, and is introduced with a photo capturing the beautiful sky that spread out in the evening. The Kaminarimon Bon Odori is a summer tradition loved by local residents and tourists, and it brightens the streets of Asakusa around this time every year. As the name Yume Toro (Dream Lanterns) suggests, the event features lantern-lit displays, and its magical atmosphere from dusk into the night is a highlight. It is run in cooperation with local merchants' associations and the Tourism Federation, and has become established as an event that marks the end of summer in Asakusa. This year again it drew large crowds, making for an evening full of Asakusa's traditional downtown charm.

122.title: Kiku Kuyo-e and the Golden Dragon Dance
122.summary: A Buddhist memorial service offering chrysanthemum flowers will be held together with the "Golden Dragon Dance."
122.body:
## Kiku Kuyo-e and the Golden Dragon Dance

On October 18, the "Kiku Kuyo-e" (Chrysanthemum Memorial Service) will be held at the Main Hall of Senso-ji Temple, together with a performance of the "Golden Dragon Dance."

The **Kiku Kuyo-e** is a long-standing event in which worshippers offer chrysanthemum flowers they have brought to Kannon, and in return receive chrysanthemum flowers said to ward off evil spirits.

The **Golden Dragon Dance** is a dance associated with the manifestation of the principal image of Senso-ji. The sight of the shimmering golden dragon parading through the temple grounds is spectacular and draws the attention of many worshippers and tourists.

Held in the clear autumn air, this event has become one of Asakusa's signature autumn traditions. Many tourists enjoy taking photos, and the area from Kaminarimon to the Main Hall becomes lively.

The temple grounds are crowded on the day, so visitors are advised to allow plenty of time.
